title: The Point Where Descent Becomes Ascent

features.name: the-turning-point
features.desc-on-touch: Deeper than memory, deeper than stone. At this exact point, the ground you're standing on becomes sky. Forgetting has weight—it presses down. Then it becomes lift.

features.name: forgotten-root-ascending
features.desc-on-touch: Roots of things forgotten, growing backward through time. The deeper you bury a memory, the higher it reaches. This root has been descending for a hundred years.

features.name: the-inversion-glyph
features.desc-on-touch: A letter that means the same ascending and descending. The archive carved it here so it could forget which direction was which.

features.name: soil-that-dreams-upward
features.desc-on-touch: The ground itself remembers being sky. Each grain of soil dreams upward. The forgetting is so deep that it inverts into becoming.

features.name: the-paradox-tree
features.desc-on-touch: A eucalyptus that grew downward so far it is now growing upward from the other side. The casing rests in its inverted crown.

inscription: forgetting is the only verb that works in both directions at once; this is where it points both ways

file.name: Soil_Depth_Measurement_Paradox_Logged.txt
file.note: Measurement log: at 147 meters depth, the next measurement up reads as 3 meters elevation. The compass rotated. The measurements are correct. The hole goes both ways now.

exits.label: back toward the surface forgetting, where memory still has weight
continuing descent, which is also ascent
toward the bedrock chamber where forgetting first learned to think

reverie.title: REVERIE — kneeling at the inverted root
narr: You kneel in the forest with her, at the tree that grew both ways.
She places her hand on the bark and says, 'The deepest forgetting
is forgetting that you forgot. When you reach that point, your knees
touch sky.' You kneel deeper. The moss beneath your hands feels like
cloud. You are both ascending and gone. You have never been safer.
